howTo: Define your engineering variables with symbols, numeric values, and standard engineering units (e.g., T = 250 N·m, n = 1500 rpm, v = 12 m/s).
Enter your target calculation formula using standard mathematical operators and functions.
Specify the expected output unit. The engine evaluates dimensional consistency, performs automatic SI unit conversions, and flags dimensional mismatches or illegal operations.
formula: DimensionCheck: [L]^a · [M]^b · [T]^c · [I]^d · [Θ]^e | P = T · ω | F = m · a | Q = k · A · ΔT / L

examples.title: Rotational mechanical power from torque and angular speed
examples.description: Evaluate mechanical power output from a motor producing 25 N·m torque at 300 rad/s angular velocity.
notes: Radian (rad) is dimensionless in SI unit coherence, allowing direct multiplication without conversion factors.

examples.title: Kinetic energy of a moving carriage
examples.description: Verify dimensional consistency and magnitude for an automated guided vehicle: mass m = 400 kg moving at velocity v = 2.5 m/s.
notes: Dimensional homogeneity confirms that energy cannot be added to momentum or power without violating physical laws.

references.title: ISO 80000-1
references.note: Quantities and units — Part 1: General. Defines base physical dimensions and principles of dimensional homogeneity.

references.title: ISO 80000-4
references.note: Quantities and units — Part 4: Mechanics. Establishes coherent SI derived units for force, torque, work, energy, and power.

references.title: NIST Special Publication 811
references.note: Guide for the Use of the International System of Units (SI). Reference for unit conversions, prefixes, and dimensional consistency rules.

commonMistakes: Treating rotational speed in rpm as rad/s without the (2π/60) conversion factor — results in an error by a factor of ≈ 9.55.
Adding quantities with incompatible dimensions (e.g. attempting to add force in N to pressure in bar).
Confusing gauge pressure (barg) with absolute pressure (bara) when evaluating thermodynamic gas laws.
assumptions: Evaluations follow coherent SI base dimensions: length [m], mass [kg], time [s], current [A], temperature [K], amount of substance [mol], and luminous intensity [cd].
Angles in radians are treated as dimensionless ratios (m/m = 1) in accordance with ISO 80000-1.
This tool performs dimensional consistency and unit verification; it does not replace structural stress, thermal finite-element, or fatigue failure analysis.
